newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker, hurt by U.S. decline.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker, hurt by U.S. decline.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened softer on Friday, hurt by weaker U.S. Treasuries, with the market largely unaffected by the Canadian employment report for June, analysts said.
"I think in the bond market it's more of a case of us following the U.S.," said Rich Wylie, a fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc. "We're actually holding in reasonably well."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.54 to C$119.25 to yield 6.525 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 17/32 to yield 6.56 percent. The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to four basis points from six at Thursday's close.
Canadian bonds weakened with U.S. Treasuries as the market there saw technical deterioration and the weight of supply from this week's refunding.

In Canada, the market had initially been focused on the release of the July jobs report. Statistics Canada this morning reported that the unemployment rate fell to 9.0 percent in July from 9.1 percent in June and employment rose by 15,000.
The report, which was weaker than expected and helped send the currency lower, did not have a substantial impact on Canadian bond prices.

While the dollar did weaken, Wylie said losses were not as great as some would have predicted given the weak report and the Bank of Canada's decision not to hike interest rates this morning. The fact that the currency's losses were limited has provided some support for bonds, he said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.22 to C$109.05 to yield 6.012 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 15/32 to yield 6.31 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 30 basis points from 28 basis points at Thursday's close.
